items.title: 2. Approval of Change Order #5 for Athletic Field Restoration at Garfield Community School with Holt Renewables, LLC.

memo.Speaker: Martín Cervantes, Bond Program Director Will Robertson, Bond Program Manager, Cumming Group
memo.Quick Summary / Abstract: The Bond Program Team requests approval of Change Order #5 with Holt Renewables, LLC ($280,866.80; +13 days) to restore the Garfield Community School athletic field outside the solar project's construction limits. Work-subcontracted to Scapes, Inc.-includes grading, debris off-hauling, irrigation repairs, sand replacement, sod installation, and initial maintenance to return the field to safe, playable condition for students and the community.
memo.Recommendation: It is the Bond Program Team's recommendation that the School Board approve Change Order #5 with Holt Renewables, LLC. for athletic field restoration at Garfield Community School.
memo.Rationale: Construction activities associated with the Garfield Community School solar project have impacted portions of the existing athletic field and turf areas. Restoration of the field is necessary to return the site to a safe, functional, and maintainable condition for student and community use. The proposed restoration work will address soil compaction, grading deficiencies, irrigation performance, and turf replacement resulting from construction activities. The scope of work includes turf removal, soil preparation, laser grading, decompaction, off-hauling of unsuitable materials, irrigation system repairs and modifications, sand testing and replacement, sod installation, and maintenance necessary to establish healthy turf growth. To complete this work, Holt Renewables, LLC. will retain Scapes, Inc., an experienced athletic field restoration contractor. Under the terms of the change order, warranties associated with irrigation, grading, grass establishment, and field restoration performance will be provided directly between the District and Scapes, Inc., ensuring accountability for the completed restoration work. Approval of this change order will allow the District to restore the athletic field to pre-construction conditions, protect the District's investment in the facility, and return the field to full operational use for students and the community.

items.title: 2. Discussion of Enrollment and Capacity Studies Community Engagement Process

memo.Speaker: Dr. Christian J. Rubalcaba, Superintendent
memo.Quick Summary / Abstract: Superintendent Dr. Christian J. Rubalcaba presents to the Redwood City School District (RCSD) Board of Trustees the community engagement process for the Enrollment and Capacity Studies. Following the Board's direction on September 23, 2026, the district will conduct two studies, each with its own engagement process and timeline. The presentation describes the two studies, how families and staff will take part, and when the Board will be asked to act. This item is for information only and does not require Board action.
memo.Rationale: Like many districts across California, RCSD has seen enrollment decline in recent years. The district enrolled about 6,244 students at the start of 2026-27, and enrollment is projected to fall to about 5,302 by 2033-34. With 12,362 seats of total facility capacity, the district uses only about half of its space, and enrollment varies considerably from school to school. This creates an opportunity to plan proactively rather than react later: to strengthen educational programs, make the best use of our schools, and be responsible stewards of the resources our community provides. Following the 2026-27 Annual Enrollment and Capacity Review, the Board approved additional analysis and community engagement. The work is guided by two goals: strengthen educational opportunities so every student has equitable access to strong instruction, programs, and support, and align our facilities with enrollment and educational needs. The district will conduct two studies, each with its own engagement process and timeline. The Capacity and Equitable Middle School Access Study for Bayside Families will examine enrollment, capacity, and equitable middle school pathways for families in the Bayside community. The Specialized Program (Orion Alternative) and Small School Study will examine long-term demand for Orion Alternative's programs and the needs of our smaller schools. Because some schools take part in both studies, staff will consider how changes in one could affect the other. For the Bayside study, the district will meet families where they are, at morning parent meetings at their own schools. For the Orion and small school study, an advisory committee of parent and staff representatives from each participating school will meet regularly. To keep the community updated, the district will communicate during the process. A dedicated webpage will hold data, materials, and summaries, and after each round of meetings the district will share a bilingual update on what was presented, what we heard, and what happens next.
memo.Financial Impact: This presentation has no financial impact.

attachments.name: Discussion of Enrollment and Capacity Study Community Engagement Process – 11.18.2026

items.title: 3. Review of Superintendent’s Listening and Learning Tour

memo.Speaker: Dr. Christian J. Rubalcaba, Superintendent
memo.Quick Summary / Abstract: Redwood City School District (RCSD) Superintendent Dr. Christian J. Rubalcaba presents to the Board of Trustees the findings of his Listening and Learning Tour, a key part of his 90-Day Entry Plan. During the tour, Dr. Rubalcaba heard directly from families and staff both in person and through an online survey. Students also participated through the survey. The presentation shares what the RCSD community values, the hopes it expressed for RCSD schools, and how those hopes connect to the district's Local Control and Accountability Plan (LCAP) goals. This item is for information only and does not require Board action.
memo.Rationale: As part of his 90-Day Entry Plan, the Superintendent launched the Listening and Learning Tour to learn from the people RCSD serves as he launched his superintendent tenure in the school district. The tour included morning sessions for families and after-school sessions for staff at every school, a session with District Office and Maintenance, Operations, and Transportation staff (MOT) and online surveys in English and Spanish for families, staff, community members, and students. What's working: Across every group, participants expressed pride in caring teachers and staff, welcoming school communities, strong communication, enrichment and language programs, and the wraparound support offered through Community Schools. Students spoke warmly and highly about their teachers, their friends, and the activities that make school a place they want to be. Opportunities to grow: Participants also shared their hopes for RCSD schools: strong support for every student, rich academic programs, well-kept campuses, fresh and healthy meals, a balanced school day, teachers and staff who stay, and clear guidance on technology. Each group emphasized different hopes, and together they offer a clear picture of what matters most to the RCSD community. Connecting to district work: Many of these hopes connect directly to the district's Local Control and Accountability Plan (LCAP) goals for engagement and school climate, English learner progress, and academic growth, and to the work already underway. Others are addressed through district operations. Questions about technology in the classroom will be taken up by an upcoming Superintendent's advisory committee. The findings have helped learn about RCSD's strengths as well as areas for opportunities.
memo.Financial Impact: This report has no financial impact.

attachments.name: Review of Superintendent's Listening and Learning Tour - 11.18.2026

items.title: 2. Approval of the Field Trip Request for Kennedy Middle School Student to Attend the Community Engagement Initiative Conference: December 3-4, 2026

memo.Speaker: Patrinia Redd, Director of Health and Wellness
memo.Quick Summary / Abstract: This board memo is seeking approval for the field trip request for the Community Engagement Initiative Conference for Kennedy Middle School. This conference will allow the Kennedy team to collaborate and implement a targeted problem of practice while building local capacity for meaningful engagement.
memo.Recommendation: It is the Administration's recommendation that the School Board approve the field trip to Anaheim, CA from December 3-4 for the Community Engagement Initiative Conference for Kennedy Middle School. This conference will allow the Kennedy team to collaborate and implement a targeted problem of practice while building local capacity for meaningful engagement.
memo.Rationale: Kennedy Middle School was selected as a Cohort VII participant for this initiative. The team will bring together district-level administrators, site administrators, teachers, a community school coordinator, a school site parent, a student, a community partner from Redwood City Together, and a representative from the San Mateo County Office of Education. Participation in the CEI Conference supports the district's goals by focusing on the following key areas: Identify effective community engagement models along with metrics to evaluate them. Build capacity within communities and school districts to lead difficult conversations centered on student outcomes. Establish strong peer-to-peer partnerships between school districts and county offices of education (CEOs) to enhance community involvement. Expand successful community engagement models across the state. Act as a facilitator, resource connector, capacity builder, and relationship builder to support school district community engagement goals. Attending this conference allows the Kennedy Middle School team to engage in an open dialogue on issues related to improving local pupil outcomes.
memo.Financial Impact: This activity will be funded by the Marin County Superintendent of Schools and the Marin County Office of Education Community Engagement Initiative.

items.title: 3. Approval of the Addendum to the Measure U Plan for Taft for the 2026-2027 School Year

memo.Speaker: David Camarena, Principal, Taft
memo.Quick Summary / Abstract: These funds support schools in strengthening core academic skills, attracting and retaining quality teachers, enhancing arts and music programs, and updating classroom technology.
memo.Recommendation: It is the Administration's recommendation that the School Board read and approve Taft's Addendum to its 2026-2027 Measure U Plan.
memo.Rationale: For Measure U, Taft was given an allotment for 2026-2027 of $90,508 and a carryover from 2025-26 of $43,594.00 for a total of $134,102.00. Taft's Site Council met on 10/26/2026 and approved its Measure U Addendum. The following are amendments proposed for Taft's Measure U Plan for the 2026-2027 school year: Increase funding from $1,100 to $5,000 for teacher release time and stipends to analyze assessment data and plan reading and mathematics instruction. Increase funding from $2,099 to $3,000 for science, math, music, PBIS, and author assemblies that enrich learning and promote a positive school culture. Increase funding from $1,000 to $4,000 for library books, materials, and reading incentives to strengthen literacy and support students in meeting their reading goals. Increase funding from $5,000 to $7,500 for field trip entrance fees and transportation to provide hands-on enrichment opportunities. Allocate $10,000 for Outdoor Education student scholarships, transportation, and teacher stipends to support access to hands-on science learning. Allocate $5,293 for teacher-led after-school tutoring to strengthen reading and mathematics skills for students needing additional support. Allocate $6,000 for weekend teacher planning and collaboration to improve instruction and support teacher retention. Allocate $4,500 for Next Gen Math for grades 3-5 and supplemental applications for second grade to strengthen mathematics skills. Allocate $2,500 for supplemental mathematics materials and workbooks to support student learning. All of the members in attendance at the 10/26/2026 School Site Council meeting voted to approve the recommendations. An updated plan for use of Measure U funds is attached for review.
memo.Financial Impact: $134,102.00 out of Measure U Site Funds

items.title: 15. Action Items (Action Required)
1. Approval of Intentional Technology for Empowered Learning Committee

memo.Speaker: Dr. Christian J. Rubalcaba, Superintendent
memo.Quick Summary / Abstract: Redwood City School District (RCSD) Superintendent Dr. Christian J. Rubalcaba presents the launch of the Intentional Technology for Empowered Learning Committee (ITELC), an advisory committee and community engagement process on technology in the classroom. Technology was one of the strongest themes in the Superintendent's Listening and Learning Tour, and families and staff asked for clear, shared guidance. The committee will develop recommendations on technology use by grade level, a technology Board Policy, and parent and staff workshops in English and Spanish. The final recommendation will come to the Board on May 26 or June 9, 2027.
memo.Recommendation: Staff recommends that the Board of Trustees receive and approve the presentation on the Intentional Technology for Empowered Learning Committee.
memo.Rationale: During the Superintendent's Listening and Learning Tour, technology emerged as one of the community's strongest themes. Families hoped for healthy limits on screen time, especially for the youngest learners. Staff asked for clear, consistent guidance on technology and AI in the classroom. In response, Superintendent Dr. Rubalcaba is forming the Intentional Technology for Empowered Learning Committee, led by two principals and made up of parents and teachers from every school, with input from students. Rather than focusing only on screen time, the committee will look at how technology can support high-quality instruction and help students create, collaborate, and think critically. The committee will meet from January to May 2027, with community surveys and a Board study session along the way. Its work will lead to recommendations on technology use by grade level, a technology Board Policy, and workshops for parents and staff. Dr. Rucalcaba will bring the final recommendation to the Board on May 26 or June 9, 2027.
memo.Financial Impact: This presentation has no immediate financial impact.

items.title: 3. Discussion and Approval of the CSBA Delegate Assembly Nominations for Region 5B

memo.Speaker: Dr. Christian J. Rubalcaba, Superintendent
memo.Quick Summary / Abstract: The California School Boards Association (CSBA) has opened nominations for the 2027-2029 Delegate Assembly term for Subregion 5B (San Mateo County), with elected trustees serving a two-year term from April 1, 2027, through March 31, 2029. Governing boards may nominate one or more eligible trustees within the region through formal board action. All board nominations and candidate acceptance materials must be certified and submitted via CSBA's electronic Simply Voting platform by Thursday, January 7, 2027. (15-min Board discussion and action)
memo.Recommendation: It is the Administration's recommendation that the Board of Education: Determine whether to nominate one or more eligible candidate(s) for the CSBA Delegate Assembly representing Subregion 5B; Take formal action by majority vote to approve the nomination(s), or take no action; and Authorize the Superintendent or Superintendent's Designee to certify the board's action and submit the approved nomination(s) via the CSBA Simply Voting electronic portal prior to the January 7, 2027, deadline.
memo.Rationale: Policy Representation & Regional Voice : The Delegate Assembly serves as CSBA's core policy-making body, establishing statewide policy platforms, electing state officers and directors, and guiding legislative advocacy on public school finance and governance. Subregion 5B encompasses San Mateo County school districts. Regional Voice : Participating in nominations ensures our region and local communities have dedicated representation advocating for public school needs at the state level. Incumbent Seats & Vacancies : Subregion 5B has three elected seats expiring on March 31, 2027, held by Gregory Land (San Mateo Union HSD), Mele Latu (Ravenswood City ESD), and Andrew Lie (Jefferson Union HSD). The remaining three elected seats in Region 5B continue through 2028. Eligibility & Selection : Any sitting trustee from a CSBA member district within Subregion 5B is eligible. Individual trustees cannot self-nominate; official ballot placement requires formal action by a member board. The Board may nominate as many eligible individuals as it deems appropriate. Nominee Commitments & Submission Protocol : CSBA conducts nominations and balloting exclusively via its Simply Voting portal. Following board nomination, each nominee must independently accept the nomination and submit biographical responses through the portal by January 7, 2027. Elected delegates are required to attend two annual meetings (scheduled for May 15-16 and November 29-30, 2027).
memo.Financial Impact: None. There is no cost associated with submitting nominations or participating in the CSBA Delegate Assembly nomination process.
